description: Pure Python library module that surfaces the OUTCOME of the most recent ZO-Sentinel gate run to the directive generator's Layer 1. Gate runs execute periodically (every 6h) via /home/workspace/zo_sentinel/tests/gates/run_gates_periodic.py invoked by gate_scheduler.py, and produce a log file under /home/workspace/logs/gate_runs/gate_run_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.log. The gate scheduler log (/home/workspace/logs/gate_scheduler.log) contains RUN_SUMMARY lines identifying the latest run's log filename and return code. Six gates currently run (1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 9): gate_1_infrastructure (service/heartbeat/table health), gate_2_schema_contracts (protected file SHA + schema contract), gate_5_synthesis_flow (canary through pivot), gate_7_threat_flow (threat association pipeline), gate_8_new_module (static_safety + import per cohort, drives quarantine), gate_9_signal_diversity (bucketed vs discriminating signals). This module reads gate outputs and produces a compact prompt-ready markdown block. It must NOT replicate the quality_map section (which already surfaces gate 8 breaker state + quarantined files via gate_quality_state.snapshot) -- gate_map is the COMPLEMENTARY summary covering the OTHER five gates. Exports SIX things: (a) GATE_RUNS_DIR = Path('/home/workspace/logs/gate_runs') as a module constant; (b) find_latest_gate_run() -> tuple[Path, datetime]|None returning the newest gate_run_*.log file by mtime, or None if directory is empty or unreadable; (c) parse_gate_log(path: Path) -> dict returning {'run_id': str, 'started_at': str, 'finished_at': str|None, 'rc': int|None, 'gates': {gate_name: {'pass': int, 'fail': int, 'novel_failures': list[str], 'known_failures': list[str], 'info_lines': list[str]}}}; the parser recognizes lines of shape '-- gate_N_<name> --' as section headers, '[ OK ] <msg>' as pass, '[FAIL] <msg>  [<code>] (known)' or '(NOVEL)' as fail with classification, '[info] <msg>' as info, and '=== Gate run <id> complete in <ms>ms ===' as terminator. Tolerate parse errors on individual lines: skip and continue, never raise. (d) summarise_gate_run(parsed: dict, max_novel: int = 5, max_known: int = 2) -> dict returning a minimal dict with keys {'run_id', 'started_at', 'rc', 'novel_failures': list[{gate, message}], 'signal_diversity': str, 'protected_file_drift': list[str], 'stale_heartbeats': list[str], 'quarantines_this_run': list[str]}; the summariser specifically extracts: from gate_7 and gate_9 the NOVEL (not known) failures; from gate_9 the 'flat=N sparse=N bucketed=N ok=N' summary line if present; from gate_2 the 'protected_file_mutated' file names; from gate_1 the 'heartbeat_stale' daemon names; from gate_8 any '[quarantine] <file>' lines. (e) build_gate_map_section(max_novel: int = 5) -> str returning a markdown block starting with '## Gate Map (last gate run)' with five subsections: '### Run metadata' (run_id, started_at, rc), '### Novel failures (warrant directive investigation)', '### Signal diversity', '### Protected file drift (gate 2)', '### Stale daemon heartbeats (gate 1)', '### Quarantines produced this run (gate 8)'. Each subsection collapses to a single '(none)' line when empty. (f) an if __name__ == '__main__' block that runs build_gate_map_section() and prints the result so 'python3 gate_map_summary.py' shows a real rendering against the latest gate run on disk, exits 0 on success and 0 if no gate runs exist (the latter prints a structured empty section with 'no gate runs found' explanation). Implementation constraints: file I/O ONLY against /home/workspace/logs/gate_runs/*.log -- no write_service calls, no network, no DB, no subprocess. Uses pathlib and re only from stdlib. Strict 5-second timeout-equivalent: if the newest log file is >50MB, read only the last 2MB via seek-from-end. Must not raise: all file errors swallowed into a graceful empty section. Output must NOT exceed 1500 chars in typical case -- truncate long novel_failure messages to 180 chars each. Scope discipline: this module is DIAGNOSTIC context for the directive generator, not an action layer. The directive generator reads gate_map alongside existing Layer 1 sections and MAY propose directives that investigate novel failures. It must NOT propose rebuilds of protected files listed in drift (that's gate 2's contract with PRODUCT_SPEC section 8) or restart directives for stale daemons (that's an ops concern, not a build concern). The rendered markdown block must end with a single scope-reminder line: 'Gate map items are diagnostic signals. Propose investigation directives for NOVEL failures only; known failures and operational gaps (stale heartbeats, protected file drift) are handled by ops runbooks, not builder directives.' Attribution in module docstring: cross-references SENTINEL_SCOPE_BOUNDARY.md Q1 (does it change what signals we extract?) -- gate_map surfaces existing gate signals that directive_gen does not yet see. Wiring into directive_knowledge_sources.assemble_layer1_context is a FOLLOW-UP directive, not this one -- the library must land, smoke, and render correctly against the real gate logs before being consumed.
context: This directive is the sibling of sentinel_intel_feed.py. Both extend Layer 1 of the directive generator (directive_knowledge_sources.assemble_layer1_context). Current Layer 1 has four sections: product_spec, wiring_map, gaps_map, quality_map. quality_map ALREADY surfaces gate 8 breaker state and quarantine list (via gate_quality_state.snapshot) -- gate_map must NOT duplicate that; it covers gates 1, 2, 5, 7, 9 complementarily. Gate log format confirmed 2026-04-22 from /home/workspace/logs/gate_runs/gate_run_20260422_124644.log: gate section headers are '-- gate_N_<name> --', pass lines begin '[ OK ]', fail lines begin '[FAIL]' with bracketed code and '(known)' or '(NOVEL)' classifier, info lines begin '[info]', quarantine events emit '[quarantine] <file> -> <path> (<n> fails)'. Six gates observed in latest run. Gate scheduler runs every 6h (POLL_SECS=21600). The quality_map concern is tracked in gate_quality_state.py; this module will source its data purely from the gate run log file on disk for three reasons: (1) gate logs are the single source of truth for all six gates including the ones that don't write DB state, (2) disk read is faster than DB query for a 100KB log, (3) it avoids coupling gate_map to write_service availability. See signal_bridge.py for the project's preferred pure-library code style; see /home/workspace/zo_sentinel/directives/cf_mcp_fingerprints.json for the sibling pattern of a scope-aware library module that's already queued. Budget: expected rendered output 500-1500 chars; total prompt size impact to directive_gen is under 2KB once wired.
